title: Linear acceleration magnitude
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be 4 m/s², derived from kinematic equations for uniformly accelerated motion from rest.

title: Centripetal force magnitude
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be approximately 1430.8 N, calculated correctly using F = m v² / r.

title: Body angle magnitude
description: Essential: The final answer for part (3) must be 27°, obtained from the inverse tangent of the ratio mg / F_centripetal.

title: Kinematic equation application
description: Important: For part (1), the student must correctly apply the equation s = (1/2) a t² for motion starting from rest.

title: Force balance reasoning
description: Important: For part (3), the student must recognize that tan θ = (gravitational force) / (centripetal force) for the described equilibrium condition.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: All calculated quantities should be presented with correct SI units (m/s², N, degrees).

title: Incorrect kinematic equation
description: Pitfall: Using v = a t or s = v t for part (1) without accounting for starting from rest, leading to a wrong acceleration.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Confusing the angle or its trigonometric function (e.g., using sin or cos instead of tan, or inverting the force ratio).
